concerns.text: FR-001 (STRING download) and FR-002 (DEG download) lack explicit task coverage for the '5-8 model organisms' scope. T012/T013 mention 'several' and 'config' but do not explicitly task the definition of the organism list or the iteration logic required to satisfy the '5-8' count constraint in FR-001.

SC-001 requires comparing results against an empirical null distribution generated by shuffling labels '[deferred]' times. T018a implements the loop but uses the placeholder '[deferred]' without assigning a concrete integer value or a task to determine this value, leaving the success criterion untestable as written.

FR-009 requires skipping PGLS if n < 10 and logging a warning. T026 covers the logic, but T024 (PGLS implementation) does not explicitly include the sample size check or the conditional skip logic in its description, creating a gap where the core implementation might fail the constraint without the separate T026 task.

FR-010 requires generating degree-preserving random graphs and comparing observed correlation against the null distribution. T019a/b/c cover generation and correlation, but there is no explicit task to perform the statistical comparison (e.g., calculating the p-value or z-score) between the observed value and the rewired null distribution, which is the core of FR-010.

FR-008 requires Benjamini-Hochberg correction for PGLS p-values. T025 implements the correction, but T024 (PGLS model) and T027 (Save results) do not explicitly mention applying or outputting the *corrected* p-values, risking that the raw p-values are saved instead of the adjusted ones required by FR-008.

T009 references 'api.opentree.org' and 'taxonomic IDs' but the URL is incomplete/placeholder in the text ('api.opentree.org'). While the task exists, the description contains a broken link/placeholder that needs fixing to be actionable.
T012 and T013 descriptions contain broken/placeholder URLs ('(e.g., `) and fallback...'). The task descriptions are malformed and need the actual API endpoints or clear instructions to be actionable.
